opex.text: Operating expenses were $59.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, up $1.5 million, from $57.8 million. This is a 2.6% increase compared to 13.7% increase in net interest income after provision for credit losses. Furthermore, this increase is primarily attributable to employee expenses, as we recognize additional expenses with higher performance payouts. Furniture and equipment costs were comparatively higher in 2026 after adding a new office in the second half of 2025 and closure of the Custar office in the third quarter of 2026. We had increases in loan expense and mortgage servicing rights amortization, which were substantially offset by decreases in consulting and professional fees among others. Consulting fees are considerably lower in 2026 versus 2025 which included one-time fees associated with data processing, but we will also be incurring additional consulting fees in the remainder of the year with a couple of projects currently in process.

costs.text: Operating expenses were $59.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, up $1.5 million, from $57.8 million. This is a 2.6% increase compared to 13.7% increase in net interest income after provision for credit losses. Furthermore, this increase is primarily attributable to employee expenses, as we recognize additional expenses with higher performance payouts. Furniture and equipment costs were comparatively higher in 2026 after adding a new office in the second half of 2025 and closure of the Custar office in the third quarter of 2026. We had increases in loan expense and mortgage servicing rights amortization, which were substantially offset by decreases in consulting and professional fees among others. Consulting fees are considerably lower in 2026 versus 2025 which included one-time fees associated with data processing, but we will also be incurring additional consulting fees in the remainder of the year with a couple of projects currently in process.

prov.text: Total provision for credit losses increased $90 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. Management continues to monitor asset quality, making adjustments to the provision as necessary, in accordance with the Bank's chosen CECL methodology. The impact of higher interest rates and inflation are taken into consideration when reviewing qualitative factors. Loan charge-offs were $15 thousand higher during the three months ended September 30, 2026 than the same period in 2025. Loan charge-offs for the current quarter were in the consumer portfolio and consumer real estate portfolio segments while 99.2% of charge-offs for the same period in 2025 were in the consumer portfolio. Of the total consumer charge-offs, $13 and $43 thousand were for automobiles and trucks for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. 2025 consumer charge-offs also included $9 thousand for recreational vehicles. Recoveries were $39 thousand higher during the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to same period in 2025 with 94.0% of total current quarter recoveries in the consumer portfolio compared to 78.7% for the same period in 2025.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expenses increased $479 thousand as compared to the same period in 2025. Salaries and wages, including normal merit increases, restricted stock expense and incentive payouts, increased $486 thousand in total. Of the total, base wages and incentive expense increased $472 thousand and $75 thousand, respectively, which was offset with increased deferred salary loans costs of $29 thousand and decreased restricted stock award expense of $32 thousand compared to 2025. Benefits increased from 2025 by $185 thousand due to increased 401k expense of $87 thousand, combined taxes and workmen's compensation of $123 thousand and miscellaneous expenses of $35 thousand offset with decreased medical expense of $58 thousand.

Net occupancy expense decreased $23 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same three months in 2025. One factor that can offset occupancy expense is the receipt by the Company of building rent as it is netted out of occupancy expense. The greatest contributor to building rent comes from the division of FM Investments within the Bank. Building rent, generated from FM Investments in lieu of commissions, increased by $60 thousand in 2026 as compared to 2025. This revenue was able to partially offset increased lease expense of $56 thousand and automobile expense of $15 thousand.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Contributing to the increased net interest income for the quarter was a decrease in interest expense of $531 thousand or 3.0% compared to third quarter 2025. Since September 30, 2025, average interest-bearing deposit balances have increased $186 million or 8.3% while the Company recognized $302 thousand less in interest expense for the most recent quarter. In September 2025, the Federal Reserve made its first rate change to the federal funds rate for 2025 with a reduction of 25 basis points

followed by reductions of 25 basis points in both October and December. In September 2026, the Federal Reserve increased the federal funds rate by 25 basis points. Deposit rates continue to be reviewed and adjusted with rate changes. The following charts demonstrate increased average interest-bearing deposit balances accounted for $1.3 million of additional interest-bearing deposit expense while rate decreases accounted for decreased interest-bearing deposit expense of $1.6 million. Noninterest-bearing average deposits balances increased $13.8 million compared to third quarter 2025. The Bank continues to focus on capturing the full customer relationship; however, it has sometimes resulted in more expensive deposits being brought in.

Interest expense on borrowed funds decreased $272 thousand in the third quarter 2026 over the same time frame in 2025 due to the repayment of FHLB advances.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense was $296 thousand higher for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025 based mainly on pretax higher earnings of $3 million. Amortization of qualified affordable housing projects caused income tax expense to increase $113 and $111 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, as presented in Note 8. Effective tax rates were 18.83% and 21.19% for 2026 and 2025, respectively. Excluding the additional $113 and $111 thousand income tax expense for the respective periods, the effective tax rates would have been 18.03% and 20.20% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text: Overall, net income in the three months ended September 30, 2026 was up $2.7 million or 30.3% to $11.5 million as compared to last year's approximately $8.9 million. The biggest contributor to the improvement was net interest income. Net interest income was up $3.0 million or 11.3% due to both increased interest income of approximately $2.5 million and decreased interest expense of $531 thousand. Provision for credit losses for loans and unfunded commitments increased $90 thousand compared to 2025. Noninterest income increased by $510 thousand which was offset with an increase of $479 thousand to noninterest expense as described above. The Company remains strong, stable, and well capitalized and has the capacity to continue to cover the increased costs of expansion. The Company is optimistic about continued improvement in profitability due to the opportunity for continued expansion in the net interest margin.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income increased slightly more than $3.0 million for the third quarter 2026 over the same time frame in 2025 due to the increase in interest income of $2.5 million combined with the interest expense decrease of $531 thousand as previously

mentioned. As the new loans added in 2025 and 2026 generate more income, management expects the benefits of the Company’s strategy of repositioning the balance sheet to increase interest income in the long run. The Company has some opportunity for improved asset yield with loans repricing in 2026 and a greater opportunity beginning in 2027 and 2028. Loans as a percentage of earning assets decreased to 81.2% in third quarter 2026 compared to 83.7% in third quarter 2025. Loans to total assets decreased to 76.8% in third quarter 2026 compared to 79.1% for the same period 2025. The percentage of earning assets to total assets remained flat at 94.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. In terms of net interest margin, the Bank recognizes competition for deposits will continue; however, there is a greater opportunity for gradual improvement with repricing loans upwards in the next year.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income was up $510 thousand, or 11.7%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 over the same time frame in 2025. Customer service fees, other service charges and fees, and loan servicing were all relatively flat compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. Interchange income increased $66 thousand for the current quarter.

The volume of total originations of loans held for sale increased while the associated gain on the sale of these loans was $45 thousand lower for the three months ended September 30, 2026 over the same period in 2025. Total originations of loans held for sale for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $21.5 million with proceeds from sale at $22.4 million for 2026 compared to 2025’s activity of $14.8 million in originations and $18.6 million in sales. The mortgages sold were both 1-4 family real estate and agricultural real estate loans originated for sale.

The cash surrender value of bank owned life insurance increased $484 thousand from the same three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in BOLI revenue was due to more investment dollars and higher earnings due to the Bank repositioning its holdings, which we expect to continue into the future.

intro.text: Farmers & Merchants Bancorp, Inc. (Company) is a bank holding company incorporated under the laws of Ohio in 1985 and elected to become a financial holding company under the Federal Reserve in 2014. Our primary subsidiary, The Farmers & Merchants State Bank (Bank) is a local independent community bank that has been primarily serving Northwest Ohio, Northeast Indiana and Southeast Michigan since 1897. Our other subsidiary, Farmers & Merchants Risk Management (Captive) was a captive insurance company formed in December 2014, located in Nevada and dissolved in December 2023. The Bank includes F&M Insurance Agency, LLC, a subsidiary offering insurance products, which was formed in November 2023. We report our financial condition and net income on a consolidated basis and have only one segment.

accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.
